memoryText: And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Ezekiel 36:26 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This verse is one of the clearest statements in the Old Testament of what God does in salvation. It describes an operation, not a program of self-improvement.

“I will give you a new heart.” Notice who is the actor: “I.” God does it. The people had been told to make themselves a new heart (Ezekiel 18:31), and they could not. Here, God promises to give one. The heart in Hebrew thought is the center of the whole person: mind, will, and emotions. Salvation reaches that deep. It is not just a change of behavior or beliefs but of the self at its center.

“And a new spirit I will put within you.” The new spirit is a new disposition, a renewed inner life. In the next verse, God clarifies that this is his own Spirit: “I will put my Spirit within you.” The new life is the life of the Holy Spirit in us.

“And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh.” The heart of stone is the natural condition of fallen humanity, hard, unresponsive to God, impossible to change by willpower. A stone cannot make itself soft. Only God can remove it.

“And give you a heart of flesh.” The heart of flesh is warm, living, and responsive. It can feel, love, trust, and obey. This is what happens at conversion and continues in sanctification. We are given hearts that want what God wants.

For the Christian, this verse is both an encouragement and a prayer. It encourages us because we do not have to manufacture our own spiritual life. It is a gift. And it is a prayer because we constantly need our hearts to be kept soft. Say it for yourself and for those you love who seem far from God. He is the one who gives hearts of flesh.
weekInReview: This week you prayed three groups of Songs of Ascents on family blessing, survival through affliction, childlike trust, and the beauty of unity. In Ezekiel, you heard the watchman called again and the people warned that they were listening to him like a song but not acting. You read God’s rebuke of the false shepherds and his promise to search for his sheep himself and to set up one shepherd, his servant David. You read the great promises of Ezekiel 36 and 37: cleansing water, a new heart and spirit, and the Spirit within us, and the valley of dry bones that live by the word and the breath. You read of Gog’s final assault and God’s victory, and then the vision of the new temple and the return of the glory by the east gate. The week taught that God himself will do what his people cannot, giving them hearts of flesh and his own Spirit, and returning to dwell among them.
reflectionQuestions: God says he will give a heart of flesh and put his Spirit within us. Where do you most need him to do this soft, living work in you?
God promises to shepherd his sheep himself, to seek the lost and bind up the injured. Which of these do you need the Shepherd to do for you right now?
Ezekiel asked whether dry bones can live, and answered, “O Lord GOD, you know.” What seems dead in your life or church that you can bring to God in that spirit?
prayerPrompts: Ask God to give you a new heart.
Ask him to remove the heart of stone in you.
Thank him for the Shepherd who seeks you.
